does: Polls the window system's events once a frame and turns them into the engine's input. For a mouse motion event it finds the event's window by the event's window id and, when that is the application's main window, writes the event's position into the engine's mouse (ls::Mouse); every motion event, whatever its window, raises the input manager's motion input. It also writes the global pointer position and whether the pointer is inside the window.

evidence.says: the branch for event type 0x400 looks the window up by the event's window id, writes the converted position through the global pointer at +0x614fb70 only when the window is the application's, and queues raw input 0x10080 in either case; the global position is written from SDL_GetGlobalMouseState before the loop and the inside flag from SDL_GetMouseFocus after each event

a motion event injected with window id 0 left the position at 0,0 and the interface reported no mouse move; with the position written into ls::Mouse first, the same injected event made the UI library raise PreviewMouseMove at that position and open the tooltip of the hotbar slot under it
